a low dose of the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor 5-aza-deoxycytidine can improve the development of cloned bovine embryos by altering donor cell characteristics without affecting the development of the resulting embryos.

a low dose (0.01 μm) of the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor, 5- azacytidine, induced cell cycle changes in donor cells, increased fusion rate of NT, and increased blastocyst rate of NT embryos without altering the DNA methylation levels of the embryos.

improving the efficiency of nuclear transfer (NT), which is a process that involves removing a nucleus from an egg and replacing it with a nucleus from another cell.
the use of 5-azadeoxycytidine (5-aza-dc) to treat donor cells before nuclear transfer.
the effect of 5-azadeoxycytidine on the characteristics of donor cell and the cloned embryo.

5-aza-C at a lower dose than used in previous studies can be used to treat donor somatic cells to reduce their DNA methylation levels and improve the development of cloned embryos.
